subject: Node warmup lag impacting reserved capacity — remediation plan & summary
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@hearthai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@hearthai.com>, Procurement <procurement@hearthai.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: spike in cold-start latency since 8/18 — urgent

Jordan —

We saw a large increase in tail latency and a few user-facing errors starting this morning around 08:50 PDT. Our telemetry shows requests to your dedicated pool returning 504s and some completions taking 6–8 seconds (previously ~200–400ms). Can you confirm whether this is related to your reserved-capacity warmup changes? We’re hitting production traffic and this is visible in our dashboards.

We need ETA on mitigation and any immediate workarounds (routing, model pin, temporary throttling). Also please share any artifacts we can attach for our SRE post-incident review.

—Samira
Senior Platform Engineer
HearthAI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hearthai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spike in cold-start latency since 8/18 — urgent

Samira —

Thanks for the heads up and sorry for the impact. Quick summary of what we’re seeing from our side: a recent change to reserved-node warmup sequencing caused a cohort of nodes to delay loading the model weights under burst conditions. That created a temporary cascade where requests were queued instead of being routed to warmed standbys.

Immediate actions we’ve taken (09:30–09:40 PDT):
- Forced an emergency warmup roll-forward for HearthAI’s reserved pool to prioritize model weight downloads.
- Opened a temporary routing rule to send new requests to the regional fallback cluster (same model, slightly lower concurrency) to reduce tail latency.
- Enabled per-tenant short-circuiting of prefix cache checks to lower request processing time while nodes finish warmup.

We expect visible improvement within 10–15 minutes as rolling warmups complete. We’ll follow up with logs and a short postincident summary when the incident is fully resolved. For now, please route customer-facing tickets to me and Mateo; we’ll coordinate the communications.

Action items for us (tracked): JB-INC-1123: revert sequencing tweak if telemetry does not stabilize; MC-INC-1124: produce warmup logs + heatmap; KI-INC-1125: add automatic fallback rule to reserved capacity config.

I’ll update you in ~30 minutes with telemetry. 

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hearthai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spike in cold-start latency since 8/18 — urgent

Samira —

Following Jordan’s mitigation, we confirmed these signals:
- Percent of requests experiencing >2s latency dropped from 22% to 3% after rerouting (09:46–09:58 PDT).
- Affected reserved nodes show delayed weight cache writes: average weight download time spiked to 7–10s for a subset of nodes due to transient registry throttling.

What we’re delivering in this email:
- Short-term: keep the temporary routing rule active for 6 hours while we monitor. If you need it lifted sooner, tell us.
- Near-term (24–48h): we’ll push a hotfix that (a) changes warmup sequencing to stagger parallel downloads and (b) adds a backoff-aware registry fetcher to avoid throttling at peak.
- Long-term: a change to the reserved-node autoscaler so it pre-warms a small percentage of nodes during known traffic windows (configurable by tenant).

Attachments: warmup_logs_20260818.zip — contains node logs and registry fetch traces; postincident-summary-heatmap.png — warmup timing heatmap.

If HearthAI legal/procurement needs formal acknowledgement (credits/SLR), Jordan — can you advise on crediting policy for this type of incident?

—Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hearthai.com>, Procurement <procurement@hearthai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spike in cold-start latency since 8/18 — urgent

Samira / Procurement —

Follow-up and postincident commitments: thank you for your patience while we stabilized your workload. Outlines below are the final items from our internal review and what we’re committing to you: 

What happened (brief): a warmup sequencing change unintentionally allowed parallel weight pulls to collide under burst, triggering registry throttling and delayed node readiness. That caused queued requests and increased tail latency for HearthAI’s reserved pool.

Customer impact: production tail latency increase for ~26 minutes (08:50–09:16 PDT), ~0.6% of HearthAI production requests returned 5xx/504 during the window. No data exposure.

Remediation completed: warmup sequencing roll-forward, temporary routing to fallback cluster, hotfix scheduled and deployed (rolled out 13:00 PDT next day) that staggers downloads and retries with exponential backoff.

Postincident deliverables (already shared or attached):
- warmup_logs_20260818.zip (attached)
- postincident summary and heatmap (attached)
- Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/postmortems/2026-08-18-node-warmup-lag

Compensation / credits: per our incident credit policy, we are offering a one-time 5% invoice credit for the August billing cycle applied to reserved capacity fees. If your procurement team needs a formal SLR or legal language, Procurement@redwood will send a statement. 

Preventative actions we will take (timeline):
- 0–24h: keep routing rule active and monitor (completed).
- 24–72h: hotfix deployment (completed 08/19 13:00 PDT).
- 1–2 weeks: autoscaler pre-warm feature gated behind tenant config (ETA 09/02).
- 30 days: internal testing & chaos test to validate warmup under sustained registry throttling (ETA 09/18).

Next steps for HearthAI: please confirm whether you want the temporary routing rule to remain for an extra 24 hours; we’ll leave it active unless we hear otherwise. Procurement — we’ll send formal credit paperwork today.

If you’d like, we can set a short 15-minute call to walk through logs and the postmortem runbook.

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
